title: ₹3,000 Crore in Six Months — Bollywood Just Had Its Most Savage First Half in History
excerpt: Ranveer Singh rewrote every record, horror became the industry’s safety net, romance clawed its way back from the dead, and the mid-budget film may be dying. The H1 2026 report card is in.
body:
The first half of 2026 didn't just break Bollywood records — it snapped them in half, set them on fire, and walked away without looking back.

As June 30 marks the official halftime of the year, the numbers are staggering. Hindi cinema's top five grossers have collectively pulled in over **₹2,800 crore worldwide** — and that's before you count films still running in theatres. But the headline number that will define this era? The **Dhurandhar** duology has crossed **₹3,000 crore worldwide**, becoming the first Indian film franchise in history to reach that milestone.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=NvI4OS53Zw8</youtube>


Three thousand crore. Two films. One franchise. One man at the centre of it all.

## Ranveer Singh and the ₹3,000-Crore Club

**Ranveer Singh** has always been Bollywood's most combustible star — the one who shows up to award shows in skirts and disappears into characters so completely you forget he's acting. But what he did with *Dhurandhar: The Revenge* was something else entirely.

Directed by **Aditya Dhar**, the sequel opened on March 19 and proceeded to demolish everything in its path. Final worldwide gross: **₹1,852 crore**. India net alone: **₹1,149 crore** — the first Hindi-original film to cross ₹1,000 crore domestically in a single language. Combined with the first film's ₹1,307 crore, the duology sits at **₹3,019 crore** — comfortably ahead of *Baahubali* (₹2,438 crore) and *Pushpa* (₹2,092 crore).

For diaspora audiences, both films are now streaming on **JioHotstar** and **Netflix**.

## The Sequel Wave That Wouldn't Stop

If Dhurandhar was the earthquake, the aftershocks were all sequels. **Border 2** kicked the year off in January with **₹464 crore worldwide** — Sunny Deol proving, once again, that patriotism plus his particular brand of fist-clenching intensity is an ATM. **Bhooth Bangla** followed in April, reuniting **Akshay Kumar** with director **Priyadarshan** for a horror-comedy that grossed **₹247 crore** and reminded everyone that these two together are cinematic gold. And **Cocktail 2**, starring **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon**, and **Rashmika Mandanna**, has crossed **₹116 crore** with plenty of runway left.

Even **Riteish Deshmukh's** directorial gamble *Raja Shivaji* — a Marathi historical mounted on a national scale — pulled in **₹130 crore**, proving regional stories can absolutely play in the multiplex mainstream.

The latest entry: **Welcome to the Jungle**, which opened June 26 and has already banked **₹71 crore in four days**, tracking for a ₹95-crore first week. Akshay Kumar is now sitting on two hits in a single half-year — something even his fiercest defenders wouldn't have predicted twelve months ago.

## Horror Is the New Safety Net — and Romance Just Woke Up

Here's the genre shift nobody saw coming. Horror has become Bollywood's most bankable mid-budget play. *Bhooth Bangla* proved it domestically. Globally, *Obsession* — a $750,000 horror film made by a 26-year-old YouTuber — crossed **$371 million**, becoming one of the highest-grossing original films of the 2020s.

Producers have taken note. According to *The Hollywood Reporter India*, horror is now what every major producer is actively commissioning. As screenwriter **Saiwyn Quadras** (*Neerja*, *Maidaan*) put it: "Genre-wise, horror is what a lot of producers are thinking of."

But the more interesting resurrection? **Romance.** *Saiyaara*, a sweeping romantic drama led by fresh faces, became an unexpected blockbuster that "caught everyone off guard." *Cocktail 2* cemented the revival. Screenwriter **Ankur Pathak** argues the industry has "almost forgotten how to make sweeping big-scale romances" — and the audience appetite is clearly ravenous.

> "Our screens have largely replaced love stories with narratives fetishising war and rewarding violence. What's needed are urban stories that reflect the lives and crisis of contemporary India — the way a *Dil Chahta Hai* or *Wake Up Sid* did." — Ankur Pathak, screenwriter

## The Streaming Reality Check

On OTT, crime and cartel dramas remain king, but breakout series like **Raakh** (Ali Fazal, Prime Video), **Chiraiya**, and **Maa Behen** showed that women-led stories can still find massive audiences. Director **Rajkumar Hirani's** first streaming project, *Pritam and Pedro*, drops on **JioHotstar** on **July 3** — a landmark signal that Bollywood's biggest names now take OTT dead seriously. For diaspora viewers, nearly every major H1 hit is now streamable across Netflix, JioHotstar, and Prime Video.

## What's Coming in H2

The second half lineup is stacked. **Alpha** (Alia Bhatt and Sharvari, **July 3**) is the first female-led spy thriller in the YRF Universe, with **Bobby Deol** as the villain and a **Hrithik Roshan** cameo. **Dhamaal 4** arrives **July 10**. **Ranbir Kapoor's** mythological epic *Ramayana* — scoring by **Hans Zimmer** and **A.R. Rahman** — targets Diwali. And **Shah Rukh Khan** has locked **Christmas 2026** for *King*, with daughter **Suhana Khan** making her debut.

If the first half was the overture, the second half is the full symphony. The only question: can anyone touch ₹3,000 crore?

## The Verdict

Bollywood's first half of 2026 was, by any measure, historic. One franchise rewrote the record books. Horror found a floor. Romance remembered it had a pulse. And the industry's sharpest writers are quietly warning that the obsession with tentpoles is killing the mid-budget film that built Hindi cinema in the first place.

The box office has never been bigger. Whether the stories can keep up — that's the cliffhanger nobody's written an ending for yet.
